content.comment_body: Hello, I have a configuration where I control a motor on Q2 using Modbus TCP. In the safety circuit, there is feedback going to I1. If I1 changes to low, I want the controller to set Q2 to low as well. How can this be set up using [product_name] [version_no]?
You just need to work out two main things: first, how to implement Modbus in [product_name], and second, how to program the motor control logic. Both can be found in the manual.

I think your question is missing important information. Why do you need to use Modbus? If you directly connect I1 to Q2, the output will follow the input—high input gives high output, and low input gives low output. In this case, you wouldn't need a controller at all. For us to provide a better example, we need clearer details about your requirements.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are discussing how to use a controller and [product_name] [version_no] alongside Modbus TCP to link safety input (I1) to motor output (Q2). There is uncertainty about why Modbus is needed for this setup, especially if a direct connection will achieve the same safety result. Some details are missing, making it hard for users to offer exact instructions within the software environment.
analysis.user_expectations: User hopes for a straightforward and dependable method to program the logic so Q2 turns low when I1 drops low, preferably with clear, step-by-step instructions relevant to their safety requirements.
